conversation.speaker: dialogue
conversation.text:
Police: When did you and Xiyuan’s mother separate?
Respondent: Our divorce... was five or six years ago.
Respondent: Am I very cruel? Abandoning my wife like that and leaving her to face the pain alone.
Respondent: But at that time, I thought separating was the best choice for both of us.
Respondent: I felt we couldn’t continue like this, so I found myself an excuse to escape from everything.
Respondent: I could no longer face her hollow eyes, because I knew nothing could ever fill that emptiness again.
Respondent: If we could have held each other and cried, comforted one another, and lived our days together, how wonderful that would have been.
Respondent: But I couldn’t spend my whole life watching her struggle in a swamp of emptiness.
Respondent: One day, I finally realized that compared to the trauma already suffered, what was even more painful was having someone by your side constantly reminding you of that trauma.
Respondent: From that day on, we decided to live our separate lives.
Respondent: We chose to avoid this pain.
Respondent: From then on, we made a clean break.
Respondent: Completely locking the doors to each other’s hearts.
